system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented Geopolitics: Economic Coercion, Financial Strain, and Hot Wars
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, stressed system in which economic coercion, financial-market volatility and localized wars interact and amplify one another. U.S. unilateral pressure (tariffs and sanctions) and an Iran confrontation are reshaping trade and maritime flows just as Treasury interventions struggle to calm a bond market rout. Concurrent kinetic escalation around Ukraine, cyber‑AI attacks, and great‑power tech rivalry are fragmenting alliances and supply chains while driving unpredictable cross‑domain spillovers.
system_description.scope: Interstate diplomacy and coercion (tariffs, sanctions), major regional conflicts (Iran, Ukraine), global financial stability (Treasury actions, bond markets), energy and maritime trade flows (Hormuz, tankers), cyber/AI and technology competition, and allied responses.
system_description.super_system: Planetary political‑economic system (global civilization interacting through states, markets, and transnational networks)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and investor networks
Regional security architectures (Middle East, Europe, East Asia)
Technology, cyber and space competition ecosystems

variables.name: Iran maritime-economic pressure
variables.description: Iran, the United States and regional states are engaged in an escalating campaign of U.S.-led financial pressure and Iranian maritime coercion that is shifting control over oil routes and commercial lifelines.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia's renewed mobilization and strikes against Ukraine, and sustained Western arms and political support for Kyiv, are altering battlefield dynamics and Europe's defence posture.

variables.name: U.S.–Canada tariff dispute
variables.description: The United States and Canada are locked in an escalating tariff showdown that is straining bilateral commerce, pressuring manufacturing decisions and testing political solidarity in North America.

variables.name: Treasury market and sovereign debt stress
variables.description: Surging U.S. yields, a record federal debt load and aggressive Treasury buyback interventions are reconfiguring global capital flows and the perceived safe‑haven status of U.S. government debt.

variables.name: U.S.–China technology rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are intensifying competition over semiconductors, AI infrastructure and export controls, reshaping industrial policy and the architecture of critical tech supply chains.
